summary.text: A left-hand reef break near Gracetown
Take-off drops you straight into the tube
Sharp reef, heavy lip. Not for beginners.

paragraphs.text: The Womb is a left-hand reef break, tucked just south of Lefthanders near Gracetown.
The take-off pitches you straight into the barrel. On a good one it spits you out the end.
It's short, under fifty metres, but it packs a punch.
At the end it can run into a wave breaking the other way. Then you either pull out or get caught in the tube.
It likes swell from the south-west, anywhere round to west-south-west.
It starts working around three to five feet and really turns on once it's over head height.
An easterly or north-easterly blows offshore here and grooms the face.
Surf it from mid to high tide.
Experienced riders. It's a bodyboarders' favourite, but brave stand-up surfers paddle out too.
Weekdays can be quiet. Weekends get crowded, so mind your manners in the line-up.
The reef is sharp and rocky and the wave is heavy: more than one pro surfer has ended up in hospital here.
It's a long walk from the car and help is a long way off. Sharks are part of life on this coast, so surf with a mate.
Turn off Caves Road onto Ellen Brook Road and follow it to the beach car park in Leeuwin-Naturaliste National Park. A small lookout lets you check the swell first.
From the beach, walk north past the Ellensbrook Bombie. Entry to the park is free, there are toilets at the car park, and dogs aren't allowed.
Just south is Ellensbrook, a homestead built from the mid-1850s on Mokidup, a Noongar camping place on Wardandi Country.

The area is now the locality of Yebble, named in 2021 for Sam Isaacs, the Noongar man who helped Grace Bussell rescue passengers from the wrecked SS Georgette in 1876. Gracetown, up the coast, is named after her.
Surf it as Shazza, T-Bone or Grommet. Take today's forecast, or set your own swell, wind and tide before you paddle out.
